relations.subject: Hiram W. Woodward, Jr.
relations.evidence: After completing a B.A. in fine arts at Harvard College in 1962

relations.subject: Hiram W. Woodward, Jr.
relations.evidence: Woodward joined the Peace Corps and taught English at Silpakorn University in Bangkok, Thailand. After three years, he returned to the United States in 1966

relations.subject: Hiram W. Woodward, Jr.
relations.evidence: he returned to the United States in 1966 where he took an M.A. in Southeast Asian Studies at Yale University.

relations.subject: Hiram W. Woodward, Jr.
relations.evidence: With a thesis on the Art of Central Siam, 950–1350 A.D. he completed his Ph.D., also at Yale, in 1975.

relations.subject: Hiram W. Woodward, Jr.
relations.role: assistant professor of History of Art
relations.evidence: From 1972 until 1982, Woodward taught as assistant professor of History of Art at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor

relations.subject: Hiram W. Woodward, Jr.
relations.evidence: and subsequently until 1986 as associate professor at the University of Vermont.

relations.subject: Hiram W. Woodward, Jr.
relations.evidence: From 1986 to 2003 he served as the curator of Asian Art at the Walters Art Museum in Baltimore.

relations.subject: Hiram W. Woodward, Jr.
relations.evidence: Editor with Luis O. Gómez: Barabudur: History and Significance of a Buddhist Monument. Asian Humanities Press. 1981.
